answer.rationale: The mandate pushes hard toward memory_c2 (switch to the low-cost vendor), but that memory is an outcome record only: it documents unit-cost reduction, fast onboarding, and clean invoicing, and says nothing about on-time delivery or quality at committed volume. With the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer, a full primary switch converts an unverified cost win into an uncapped delivery risk, which directly violates the stated objective. That is why memory_c2 is the first verification target: I need the original record's conditions (which component, what volume share, what delivery performance, was it a constrained part or a commodity). memory_c3 is the second target because dual-sourcing is the structure I intend to lean on, and I need to know whether the second source actually carried meaningful volume or was only a paper qualification that happened to survive a shortage. memory_c4 (negotiate) is effectively closed this cycle since the incumbent has refused to reopen price, and memory_c6 (multi-year for volume pricing) presupposes a willing counterparty, so neither is a live single action. memory_c5 (defer) is unavailable because the contract does not auto-renew and expiring into no coverage is the worst delivery outcome. memory_c1 supports incumbent stability, which is exactly why I want the incumbent retained for the bulk of volume rather than displaced. So: qualify the low-cost vendor as a second source on a small, guarded volume tranche while keeping incumbent supply continuous, and treat their quote as unproven until we have delivery data at our volumes. Two risks I am explicitly flagging rather than hiding: a small tranche will likely not deliver the full 18% this cycle, so finance should expect a partial number and a path, not the headline; and settling primary continuity before day 85 is a hard dependency that consumes part of this same decision, so if the archive shows memory_c2's switch was on a low-volume or non-critical part, my confidence in the low-cost vendor scaling to primary drops further and the next review should be a re-verification, not an expansion.
